result.title: Inject Where It Matters: Objective-Dependent Feature Control in Rectified-Flow Image Editing
result.comment: Accepted as a poster at the Principles of Generative Modeling (PriGM) Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Many prompt-driven FLUX editing methods rely on injecting source features into target-conditioned generation, creating an inherent trade-off between source preservation and the desired edit. We address this problem by controlling where source features are injected and which transformer blocks are used. First, we introduce adaptive masks that spatially gate feature injection using differences between source- and target-conditioned block outputs at matched inversion states. Second, we use REINFORCE to select Top-K injection blocks under different preservation-editability objectives. The selected blocks are fixed at inference and require no online search. On PIE-Bench with FLUX.1-dev, spatial masking controls the alignment-preservation trade-off. On 60 validation examples, a learned nine-block set gives lower whole-image LPIPS than the 18-block RF-Edit set within the same masked pipeline, with slightly lower alignment. Among 50 random nine-block sets, it has the lowest LPIPS but not the highest reward. Separate objective sweeps reveal different block preferences for preservation and alignment.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 FLUX 提示驱动图像编辑中源特征注入的位置与层选择问题：用源/目标条件下匹配反转状态的块输出差异构造自适应空间掩码来门控注入，并用 REINFORCE 在不同保真—可编辑目标下挑选 Top-K 注入块，选定后推理期固定。
AI.relevance_reason: 按目标选择「注入哪些层、在何处注入视觉特征」的离线搜索加固定推理策略，或可迁移为 LVR 中视觉证据写入位置与层选择的可核查线索；但属图像编辑生成场景，与多模态推理状态无直接关系。
